curatorNote: Transcribed from the Arizona Secretary of State's partisan candidate filing for the 2026 primary and the Legislative Council's 2026 ballot-measure analyses, then extended on 2026-08-27 from three documents the earlier curation did not have: the Pima County Official Candidate List for the July 21 primary (the county's own record of what was PRINTED, which unlike the canvass includes uncontested races), the certified Pima County primary canvass of 2026-07-30 (which names the winners and is the only document carrying party), and the Pima County School Superintendent's 2026 School District Special Elections page (which numbers the local propositions). measures.questionText: Pursuant to the Arizona State Constitution, Pima County seeks voter approval to permanently adjust the expenditure base of the County as determined by the Economic Estimates Commission. The County seeks an adjustment of $70,000,000. A “YES” vote shall have the effect of allowing Pima County to adjust its 1979-80 base expenditure limit. A “NO” vote shall have the effect of not allowing Pima County to adjust its 1979-80 base expenditure limit.
measures.officialStatement: Official Title: A resolution proposing a permanent adjustment to the state-imposed 1979-80 expenditure base for Pima County. Summary analysis: if approved, the County’s 1979-80 base expenditure limitation will be increased by $70,000,000 adjusted each future year for population and inflation growth since 1979-80. With voter approval, in fiscal year 2027-2028 the County’s expenditure limitation will increase by $610,086,481, from $817,131,286 to $1,427,217,767. Referred to the people by the Pima County Board of Supervisors by resolution 2026-23, passed 2026-04-21.

provenance.sourceOrg: Pima County, Permanent Base Adjustment — Ballot Language

measures.questionText: BUDGET OVERRIDE CONTINUATION, YES / NO — whether Vail Unified School District No. 20 of Pima County, Arizona may continue to exceed the revenue control limit by not more than 12.5% per fiscal year, for fiscal years 2027/2028 and the next six fiscal years.
measures.officialStatement: From the district’s statutory Notice of Election: a special election consolidated with the General Election of November 3, 2026, under A.R.S. § 15-481(P). The budget effect is approximately $5,102,762 above the alternate budget for 2027/2028, at an estimated continuation of $1.61 per $100 of secondary assessed valuation. The governing board adopted the calling resolution on 2026-06-02. Arguments were due to the Pima County School Superintendent by 5:00 p.m. on 2026-08-07.

provenance.sourceOrg: Pima County School Superintendent, 2026 School District Special Elections (proposition number); Vail Unified School District No. 20 Notice of Election (question and fiscal terms)

coverageNotes: Proposition 427, a $250,000,000 bond for Pima County Joint Technical Education District No. 11, is on the ballot of every voter in that district — which includes all of ZIP 85641 — and is not shown as a contest because no division in this registry matches the district's territory. Measured 2026-08-27 against the county's own JTED layer: the district covers about 73% of Pima County AND contains sampled points in Pinal County, so attaching it to the county would both show it to voters who do not vote on it and hide it from voters who do. Its estimated average tax rate is $0.14 per $100 of net assessed limited property value; its question text is not published — the district's Request for Arguments says the text is available by request from the district at 2855 West Master Pieces Drive, Tucson.

Justice of the Peace and Constable are elected by justice precinct, and this registry has no justice-precinct division. ZIP 85641 spans Precincts 7 and 8. On the November 3, 2026 ballot, Precinct 7 elects a Justice of the Peace (Raymond Carroll won the Republican primary 7,077 to Kara Egbert's 4,773; no Democrat filed) and Precinct 8 elects a Justice of the Peace (Kristel Ann Foster, Democratic, and William Parven, Republican). Neither precinct has a Constable race this cycle: the only Constable contests on the county's official candidate list are Precincts 2, 3 and 9.

Pima County's elected county offices — Sheriff, Assessor, Recorder, Treasurer, County Attorney, School Superintendent — and Board of Supervisors Districts 2 and 4 are NOT on the November 3, 2026 ballot. This is read from the county's Official Candidate List, which prints uncontested races and lists only Board of Supervisors District 5 among supervisor seats; it is not a gap in this file.
